curated.instructions: omr/instructions/42083-1-1.pdf (book 1: chassis, gearbox, W16 engine, steering and paddle shifters) and omr/instructions/42083-1-2.pdf (book 2: body, rear wing, doors, wheels, key and bag); page numbers are the PDF's

functions.does: The steering wheel steers the front wheels: its column runs forward along the cockpit's left side to bevel gears under the nose, and a shaft down the middle turns the pinion on the steering rack.
functions.source: book: book 1 steps 266-285 (front axle, rack and steering links) and 343-375 (column and gears); the finished model on book 2 page 315

functions.does: The two paddle shifters behind the steering wheel shift the 8-speed sequential gearbox one gear up or down: they sit on one rocker, which pushes a pawl round a pin wheel a quarter turn per click, and that turn is carried back to the gearbox, where two rotary catches slide its driving rings in turn.
functions.source: book: book 1 steps 351-359 (the pin wheel, pawls and paddle rocker, page 225's inset) and 88-117 (the gearbox, with its rotary catches); inferred: which paddle shifts up, and how the pin wheel's turn reaches the gearbox (the steps don't say in words)
functions.note: a ratcheting stepper: each paddle press should advance the pin wheel by one pin and spring back, rather than following a plain drag

functions.does: Two rubber bands in the paddle mechanism bring the rocker and its pawls back after each shift.
functions.source: book: book 1 steps 351-359; inferred: exactly what each band pulls
functions.skip: a spring: only matters under force

functions.does: Rolling the car runs the W16 engine: all four wheels are driven, each axle through its own differential, and a shaft between them turns the gearbox, whose output turns the engine's three crankshafts so the sixteen pistons run up and down in their four banks, faster in the low gears.
functions.source: book: book 1 steps 13-64 (rear axle and differential), 88-141 (gearbox), 142-199 (engine) and 254-292 (front axle and differential); inferred: the ratios in each gear
functions.note: some gear is always engaged (there's no neutral in the book), so the engine always turns with the wheels

functions.does: Each axle's differential lets its two wheels turn at different speeds, as in a corner.

The speed key raises and lowers the rear wing: its long axle goes into a hole behind the left rear wheel, into the shaft under the wing, and turning the key swings the wing up on its arms or folds it down flat.
functions.source: book: book 2 steps 965-968 (the key) and page 310 (key in place, arrows on the key and the wing); 480-554 (wing and its shaft); inferred: which way of turning raises it, and whether the wing also tilts
functions.note: in the file the key (its axle is p3540 23948) lies on the ground beside the left rear wheel rather than in its hole, which is p2099 59443

functions.does: The two doors swing open on hinges at their front edges.
functions.source: book: book 2 steps 931-943 (doors); the finished model on page 315

functions.does: Each front wheel has independent suspension: its steering knuckle rides between a lower and an upper suspension arm, with two shock absorbers, so the wheel can rise and fall.
Each rear wheel has independent suspension in the same way: its upright rides between two arms, with two shock absorbers.
functions.source: book: book 1 steps 28-47 (rear wheel supports and shock absorbers)

functions.does: The shock absorbers' springs hold the car up and spring back.
functions.source: book: book 1 steps 39-40 (rear) and the front axle steps
functions.skip: a spring: only matters under force

functions.does: The Bugatti overnight bag sits in the storage space at the front, behind the grille.
functions.note: a loose piece of luggage, not a mechanism; listed so it isn't taken for a missing part

questions.question: How many gears, and which paddle shifts up? Does the 42083's wing tilt as it rises, and its front hood open?
